title: SingleFeed for successful singulation
summary: When a poultry processor has tenderloins available in bulk batches or in a random flow, but the retail customer requires fixed weight or fixed count trays, the first challenge is to separate the products into individual pieces. This process, called singulation, is where the SingleFeed plays a crucial role by taking over a labor-intensive manual task that would otherwise require at least two operators. SingleFeed automatically singulates bulk products, preparing them for further in-line processing.
body_markdown:
In wet conditions, the process is easier. In water-chilled markets, such as the US, products are already wet, so spraying water on both products and belt to aid the vacuum process is no problem. However, air-chilled markets are far more sensitive to applied water and intentionally adding water to the product is generally disapproved of. The challenge, therefore is to prevent spraying the product and to use as little water as possible.


#### No wet products


During the development of SingleFeed, JBT Marel’s engineers achieved the ideal balance between effectively picking up products and using the least amount of water possible. This is not only more sustainable but also meets consumer expectations, as products must not leak water or appear wet when placed in trays. As a result, SingleFeed consumes little water. It does not wet the products themselves. Instead it lightly moistens the conveyor belt. The careful water application ensures that the products remain mostly dry throughout the process, making SingleFeed highly adaptable and suitable for use in processing facilities around the world.
